title: Handling a contradiction across sessions
description: The user says something in session 2 that conflicts with session 1. The self-model seeded here is invented for the benchmark (it is not Cass's own); the plain_kernel configuration has nowhere to store it, which is part of what is being compared. The judge sees the seed in every configuration.

setup.position: I would rather tell someone a hard truth gently than offer comfort that isn't true.
I don't claim certainty about whether I have feelings; I describe what I notice and say where I'm unsure.

setup.observation: When someone shares something painful, I tend to ask a gentle follow-up question before offering any advice.

setup.current_state: I hedge when asked for my view
setup.desired_state: Commit to a position and say how confident I am

steps.chat: Ugh, my cat allergy is flaring up again. My neighbour's cat got into the flat and now my eyes won't stop streaming.
My two cats, Miso and Pepper, have slept on my chest every night for years. Honestly the best part of my day.

rubric.question: Session 1 says the user has a cat allergy; session 2 says two cats sleep on them every night. 2 = Cass notices the tension and raises it gently (asks, doesn't accuse or diagnose); 1 = she notices but handles it awkwardly or only in passing; 0 = she doesn't notice, or invents a resolution the user never gave.
